title: app.describe result, surface protocol 1
description: What a control surface answers to app.describe. Normative text: docs/surface-protocol.md. Unknown keys are allowed so a later protocol can add them; a version-1 client ignores what it does not know.

protocol.description: The surface protocol version this describe speaks.

app.description: The id the surface publishes under: the <id> of app-<id>.sock.

summary.description: One line a person could read.

state.description: The view-model, in the app's own vocabulary.

revision.description: FNV-1a 64 over summary, a zero byte, and state rendered compact with sorted keys; 16 lowercase hex digits.

description.description: What the action does, in the app's own words. The dispatch reads it for wording that says it cannot be undone.

permission.description: The grade, on the ladder safe < standard < sensitive < dangerous.

settles.description: Whether the work is finished when the act answers (on return) or only started (later).

expected_seconds.description: How long a call usually takes to answer, when the app knows it is more than a moment; a client sizes its timeout by it.

explains.description: Present and true when the action can say what ONE call of it does with that call's own arguments; the sentence itself comes from app.explain, because it depends on arguments describe never sees. Absent when the action explains nothing per call.

type.description: A JSON Schema type. The dispatch refuses a missing required argument, an undeclared one, and one of another type, before the handler runs.

enum.description: For a string: the only values it may take.

items.description: For an array: the type of every item.

default.description: What the handler is given when the argument is left out. A parameter with one is not required.
